question: Should explicit requester consumption of descendant output count as durable delivery proof that suppresses later descendant retry/finalization for this PR?
rationale: The code path is focused, but it changes the product boundary between visible descendant delivery, requester-consumed delivery, and durable retry/spool behavior; automation cannot infer that policy choice from tests alone.

options.title: Require proof and semantic sign-off
options.body: Keep the PR open until it is rebased, real behavior proof is posted, and maintainers explicitly accept the requester-consumed delivery boundary.

options.title: Accept the boundary after rebase
options.body: Maintainers can decide that exact matched requester consumption is sufficient delivery proof and treat remaining risk as an intentional lifecycle tradeoff.

options.title: Fold into durable inbox work
options.body: If requester consumption is not the desired proof boundary, pause or close this PR and solve the case in the broader durable completion inbox/spool design.

recommendation.title: Require proof and semantic sign-off
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open until it is rebased, real behavior proof is posted, and maintainers explicitly accept the requester-consumed delivery boundary.
